title: Directions (Q71-74): Read the table of modern navigation methods and answer the questions
passage:
| Method | Description | Application |
|---|---|---|
| Dead reckoning | Advances a prior position using the ship's course and speed; the new position is a DR position. Correcting it for leeway, current effects and steering error gives an estimated position (EP). | Used at all times |
| Pilotage | Navigating in restricted waters with frequent determination of position relative to geographic and hydrographic features. | When within sight of land |
| Celestial navigation | Reducing celestial measurements to lines of position using tables, spherical trigonometry and almanacs. | Used primarily as a backup to satellite and other electronic systems in the open ocean |
| Radio navigation | Uses radio waves to determine position, by radio direction finding or hyperbolic systems such as Decca, Omega and LORAN-C. | Losing ground to GPS |
| Radar navigation | Uses radar to determine distance from or bearing of objects whose position is known. | Primarily when within radar range of land |
| Satellite navigation | Uses artificial Earth satellite systems, such as GPS. | Used in all situations |
